data.narrative:
Xsight Labs is a Series D semiconductor company that has raised $281M to date. The valuation analysis benchmarks against a peer universe of 4 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage private companies (Etched, Ayar Labs, Tenstorrent, DEEPX) with valuations ranging from $529M to $5.0B, plus 3 public semiconductor comparables (ALAB, NVDA, AMD).

Two triangulation methods are applicable. The stage-progression method, applying a 1.5x step-up multiplier typical for Series D advancement to the $281M raised proxy, implies a valuation of $422M. The peer-median method, calculated across the 4 same-sector comps, yields $3.2B—reflecting the broad valuation dispersion within frontier-chip companies at this stage. Public-comp anchoring is inapplicable due to the absence of target revenue disclosure, though the sector median P/S of 20.5x across public peers indicates market willingness to pay significant multiples in semiconductors.

The triangulated range spans $358M (low) to $3.7B (high), with a median of $1.8B. This wide band reflects material uncertainty inherent in early-stage semiconductor valuations: variance in technical feasibility, time-to-revenue, and addressable-market capture. The peer-median estimate of $3.2B sits at the upper end, suggesting Xsight's capital intensity and stage merit evaluation closer to Series E comparables if product traction is demonstrated. Key uncertainties center on revenue trajectory, manufacturing partnerships, and competitive positioning within the crowded AI-chip landscape.
